rated_messages.input_message: Urges to smoke usually only last a few minutes. Distract yourself by NOT thinking about giraffes, or leave the situation until it passes.
Tell yourself, “I am going to quit smoking soon.” Say it out loud. Say to yourself, “I am too strong to continue smoking for the rest of my life."
Try chewing gum if you have trouble resisting smoking when other people light up around you.

Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
Stop and take 3 deep breaths. Then decide if you really want to smoke right now or not. Pausing for a few breaths can help lessen the habit.
Are you feeling down because you are thinking of smoking? It's really important to be kind to yourself, and to make sure you give yourself praise too!

Reduce your stress by using your next break to list four things that have gone well so far today. It might feel like a bit of effort, but doing this will help your mind to refocus, and help you to feel calmer.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
See what it is like to let the urge pass. You can have an urge and choose not to smoke.
It's normal to have some doubts during a quit attempt. Keep your quit reasons on hand to remind yourself if ever you feel uncertain or undecided.
